sources.title: Socio-Economic Effects of El Niño in Malawi: Implications for Recovery and Long-Term Resilience Building
sources.organization: United Nations Malawi and Government of Malawi partners
sources.temporal_coverage: Assessment of the 2023/24 El Niño drought and floods, with outlook material published in 2024.
sources.methodology: UN–government synthesis of crop, education, nutrition and protection sources.
sources.limitations: Secondary synthesis; GBV may be underreported.

sources.title: United Nations Common Country Analysis: Malawi 2024 Update
sources.organization: United Nations Country Team in Malawi
sources.temporal_coverage: Country analysis updated in 2024; mobility and displacement passages include 2022–2024 events.
sources.methodology: UNCT synthesis of national data and consultations.
sources.limitations: Secondary evidence; some estimates lack district detail.

sources.title: State of Malawi Climate in 2024
sources.organization: Department of Climate Change and Meteorological Services, Government of Malawi
sources.temporal_coverage: Meteorological observations and reported disaster impacts for calendar year and rainy season 2023/24.
sources.methodology: National weather-station analysis and Department of Disaster Management Affairs incident data.
sources.limitations: Station-based meteorological drought is not the same as agricultural or hydrological drought; disaster counts are reported figures.

sources.title: 2024 UN Country Results Report
sources.organization: United Nations Country Team in Malawi
geographic_coverage: Dzaleka refugee camp and host community
sources.temporal_coverage: Reports on UN Country Framework results and programme outputs during 2024.
sources.methodology: UN agency self-reporting of 2024 programme outputs and results.
sources.limitations: Not an independent impact evaluation; reported outputs do not establish effectiveness. Report publication date is unstated.

sources.title: Malawi Humanitarian Situation Report No. 4, 31 December 2025
sources.temporal_coverage: Operational and needs update for 1 January–31 December 2025; cover dated 26 January 2026.
sources.methodology: UNICEF operational situation report based on programme monitoring and humanitarian response reporting.
sources.limitations: Historical 2025 snapshot; service outputs are not impact evaluations or evidence of current 2026 conditions.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 33–34 (PDF pp. 47–48), 2023/24 drought conditions and Figure 21.
claims.paraphrase: In the 2023/24 season, meteorological drought lasted five months in Machinga, Mangochi, Zomba and Chikwawa, and four months in Chitipa, Nsanje, Dedza, Phalombe, Chiradzulu and Thyolo; additional southern and central districts had dry spells through much of the season.
institutions: Department of Climate Change and Meteorological Services
claims.limitations: The report's station-based measure is meteorological drought, not measured crop or groundwater impact.

claims.locator: Printed p. 37 (PDF p. 51), section 5.0, 2023/24 affected-household summary.
claims.paraphrase: For the 2023/24 season, DoDMA data in the report count 17,033 households affected by floods in Karonga and Nkhotakota; all recorded hazards affected 21,333 households.
claims.limitations: The report relays DoDMA counts and does not attribute these particular floods to climate change.

claims.locator: Printed p. 23 (PDF p. 23), section 4.2.2, education and child protection.
claims.paraphrase: The assessment links El Niño income stress to children joining guardians' casual work, school absenteeism and child labour.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Economic stress is linked to child-protection harm.

claims.locator: Printed p. 24 (PDF p. 24), section 4.2.3, cited El Niño Rapid Gender Analysis.
claims.paraphrase: The cited analysis reports violence against women and girls doubling in most affected districts; Machinga recorded 286 child marriages in January–May 2024 versus 162 a year earlier.
institutions: Ministry of Gender, Community Development and Social Welfare
claims.limitations: Rapid gender analysis; weak services may mean underreporting.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Food insecurity and economic vulnerability link to child marriage.

claims.locator: Printed p. 25 (PDF p. 24), section 4.2.4, El Niño Rapid Gender Analysis findings.
claims.paraphrase: Drought lengthened women's water-collection journeys; women, girls and people with disabilities were excluded from key response-governance structures.
claims.limitations: No districts are named for these findings.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Drought burdens and response exclusion are reported together.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 40–41 (PDF pp. 48–49), section 3.1.11, internally displaced people.
claims.paraphrase: The CCA reports 20,000+ people displaced by March 2024 floods in Karonga and Nkhotakota; about 400 households remained displaced in Nsanje, Chikwawa, Zomba and Nkhotakota; early camp closures prompted returns to unrepaired, flood-exposed homes.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Early returns left households exposed to floods.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 41–42 (PDF pp. 48–49), section 3.1.11, drought-related mobility.
claims.paraphrase: After dry spells and food insecurity, mostly male members of drought-affected Southern Region households moved semi-voluntarily for casual work in Blantyre, Mzuzu, Lilongwe, Rumphi or Mzimba.
claims.limitations: Movements are sporadic and difficult to quantify.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Food insecurity is a stated mobility driver.

claims.locator: Printed p. 76 (PDF pp. 83–84), climate-change analysis, climate-induced migration passage.
claims.paraphrase: The CCA warns climate-driven mobility may intensify scarce-land competition and migrant–host tensions; it also reports households moving for arable land and fishers seeking grounds along Lake Malawi.
claims.scenario: Conditional pathway; no quantified scenario or timeline stated.
claims.limitations: Not measured climate-caused conflict; no local districts specified.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Climate mobility may heighten intercommunal tensions.

claims.locator: Printed p. 18 (PDF p. 18), 2024 food-security results for Dzaleka camp and host community.
claims.paraphrase: WFP and UNHCR reported that about 4,000 households affected by El Niño in Dzaleka refugee camp and its host community received a US$400,000 parametric-insurance payout in 2024.
institutions: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
claims.limitations: The results report records a payout, not its adequacy or effects on food security.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The reported El Niño payout explicitly covered refugee-camp and host-community households.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 21–22 (PDF pp. 21–22), output 4.2, strengthening duty-bearer capacities.
claims.paraphrase: In 2024, IOM and UNDP integrated climate risk into 23 district development and contingency plans; UNEP trained 136 district-planning members, while a local climate-risk mapping tool remained under development.
claims.limitations: UN-reported activities and training are outputs; the mapping tool was not yet complete.

claims.locator: Printed p. 21 (PDF p. 21), response to capacity gaps identified in the Cyclone Freddy and Cholera After-Action Review.
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF reported training over 60 district disaster-risk-management staff in risk analysis, response planning, gender, GBV and protection from exploitation after an after-action review identified weak government capacity.
claims.limitations: Training is a reported capacity output; the report does not assess resulting performance.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The report ties training to weak capacity revealed by the Freddy and cholera after-action review.

claims.locator: Printed p. 2 (PDF p. 1), 2025 food insecurity and nutrition; district results for January–September.
claims.paraphrase: In 2025, severe-wasting admissions exceeded projections in 11 districts, with the largest increases in Neno (135%), Nsanje (123%) and Chikwawa (97%); UNICEF also cited erratic rainfall and cyclone damage among food-insecurity drivers.
claims.limitations: The annual humanitarian report lists multiple drivers, including economic conditions; it does not attribute district nutrition changes to climate alone.

claims.locator: Printed p. 3 (PDF p. 3), WASH response results for 2025.
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF reported deep-water systems in drought-affected schools and communities in Nsanje and Neno reaching over 12,000 people, more than half women and girls; improved sanitation reached 36,569 people in Chikwawa and Nsanje.
claims.limitations: Reported reach is a service-output measure and does not establish durability or health impacts.

search_audit.query: Malawi climate drought flood district 2024 2025 official report named districts UN government PDF
search_audit.outcome: Located and directly opened the Malawi State of Climate report, UN Common Country Analysis and El Niño assessment; retained named districts and dated exposures.

search_audit.query: Malawi climate conflict land resource tensions districts refugees floods drought UN report 2024 2025 PDF
search_audit.outcome: The opened UN reports describe child-labour coping, protection and gender risks, flood displacement, drought-related mobility and a conditional land-competition pathway.

search_audit.query: site:malawi.un.org Malawi climate disaster displacement district 2025 report conflict peacebuilding
search_audit.outcome: The UN Country Results Report documents El Niño support for refugee-camp and host households in Dzaleka; flood-displaced households returned to locations still exposed to flood risk.

search_audit.query: Malawi climate preparedness resilience local disaster capacity District Development Plans 2024 2025 UN report
search_audit.outcome: The opened UN 2024 results and UNICEF 2025 operational report document district planning, staff training, early warning and water-service outputs; effectiveness is not independently assessed.

gaps: No inspected source establishes climate as a cause of armed violence in Malawi; the CCA's future host–migrant tension pathway is conditional, not an incident-level finding.
Protection and GBV findings in the 2024 El Niño assessment are secondary synthesis and may be underreported; named-district detail is limited.
The 2024 UN Country Results Report and 2025 UNICEF report describe outputs and historical conditions, not evaluated effects or current 2026 coverage.
The CCA identifies climate-related mobility and land competition but does not quantify future conflict risk by district or provide a climate scenario.
